page: Microsoft Azure E192ids_v6 is an isolated, memory-optimized instance from the Edsv6 series, engineered for large-scale enterprise workloads requiring substantial memory density and high-throughput local I/O. The system provides 192 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 96 physical cores on an Intel Xeon 8573C processor running at up to 4.2 GHz. It integrates 260 MB of L3 cache alongside advanced hardware vector extensions, including AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX). Memory capacity totals 1,832 GB, providing approximately 9.54 GB of RAM per vCPU. The instance includes 11,339 GB of fast local NVMe SSD storage, while operating without discrete hardware accelerators or GPUs.

Benchmark measurements indicate exceptional multi-threaded computational and memory subsystem throughput. In stress-ng multi-core testing, the instance achieved 158,923.19 points, positioning it in the top tier. Uncached memory read bandwidth reached 430.1 GB/sec, while uncached write bandwidth achieved 187.08 GB/sec. This translates into high transaction capabilities, reflected in PassMark database operations scoring 35,481.69 and Redis throughput reaching 179.31 million SET operations per second. Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression and Clang software compilation also registered in the top 10% of benchmarks. Single-thread execution sits in the average to strong tiers, confirming that aggregate scale rather than single-core frequency defines the system's performance envelope.

Resource allocation presents a specific tradeoff balance. While the instance provides high compute and memory capacity on a single node, single-threaded task performance does not lead its class, making it less optimal for workloads bounded by single-core bottlenecks. The lack of complimentary public IPv4 addresses requires explicit virtual network routing. However, for organizations consolidating multiple database nodes or scaling large in-memory footprints, the combination of 1.8 TB RAM and 11.3 TB of high-speed local NVMe yields high resource density and qualitative cost efficiency over maintaining fragmented clusters.

The hardware configuration is well-suited for high-throughput in-memory caching systems, large relational and NoSQL databases like SAP HANA, SQL Server, and Redis clusters, enterprise ETL pipelines, and high-concurrency static web serving.
description: Microsoft Azure E192ids_v6 is an isolated, memory-optimized virtual machine designed for high-density enterprise computing. Powered by a 96-core Intel Xeon 8573C processor delivering 192 dedicated vCPUs at up to 4.2 GHz, the instance features 260 MB of L3 cache and supports Intel AMX and AVX-512 instruction sets. It includes 1,832 GB of system memory, yielding roughly 9.54 GB per vCPU, and bundles 11,339 GB of local NVMe SSD storage without integrated GPUs. Benchmark evaluations show top-tier multi-threaded compute, memory bandwidth, and caching capabilities, demonstrated by 179.31 million Redis SET operations per second and high uncached read throughput of 430.1 GB/sec. While single-thread execution is standard, the massive parallel capacity delivers strong resource efficiency when consolidating large systems. The instance is suited for in-memory databases, large data warehousing engines, Redis clusters, and concurrent transactional databases.
